name: IMF Canada: 2025 Article IV Consultation – Press Release and Staff Report
desc: IMF staff country report providing macro assessment, GDP trajectory, fiscal balance, monetary policy, trade exposure, and structural reform analysis for Canada as of January 2026.

name: Bank of Canada Monetary Policy Report – April 2026
desc: Official BoC quarterly outlook covering GDP growth projections (1.2% in 2026), inflation (3.2% near-term, easing to 2% in 2027), policy rate held at 2.25%, and trade-uncertainty risks.

name: Statistics Canada – The Daily: GDP, Income and Expenditure, Q1 2026
desc: Official quarterly national accounts release showing real GDP was unchanged in Q1 2026 after a 0.2% decline in Q4 2025, providing the latest output performance figures.

name: Global Affairs Canada – Canada's State of Trade 2025
desc: Annual government trade report documenting Canada's export ($997B) and import ($1T+) totals for 2024, sector performance, and partner concentration, with SME focus.

name: Global Affairs Canada – Quarterly Economic and Trade Report: Spring 2026
desc: Quarterly government report confirming real GDP grew 1.7% in full-year 2025, Q4 2025 contraction of 0.6% (annualized), and BoC projection of 1.1% growth in 2026.

name: Government of Canada – Spring Economic Update 2026: Economic and Fiscal Overview
desc: Official federal fiscal update projecting a $65.3B deficit (1.9% of GDP) for FY2026-27, declining deficit track, and nominal GDP growth assumptions for Canada.

name: Parliamentary Budget Office – Economic and Fiscal Outlook, June 2026
desc: Independent federal fiscal watchdog report projecting a $72B deficit (2.2% of GDP) in 2025-26, real GDP growth of 1.1% in 2026, with US tariffs treated as permanent.

name: OECD Economic Outlook, Volume 2026 Issue 1 (June 2026)
desc: OECD flagship outlook forecasting Canada's GDP growth at 1.2% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, with analysis of tariff headwinds, household consumption, and energy sector as growth driver.

name: Statistics Canada – The Daily: Consumer Price Index, May 2026
desc: Official CPI release showing Canada's headline inflation rose to 3.2% year-over-year in May 2026, driven by gasoline (+33.2% y/y) and food price acceleration.

name: Statistics Canada – The Daily: Labour Force Survey, May 2026
desc: Monthly labour market release showing employment rose 88,000 (+0.4%) in May 2026, unemployment rate fell to 6.6%, and employment rate reached 60.7%.

name: Statistics Canada – Population Estimates, Quarterly (Table 17-10-0009-01)
desc: Official quarterly population estimates showing Canada's population at 41,472,081 as of Q1 2026, confirming the first annual population decline in Canadian history in 2025.

name: Statistics Canada – The Daily: Population Estimates: Age and Gender, July 1, 2025
desc: Official age-structure release confirming Canada's population of 41,651,653 on July 1, 2025 and updated median age data showing aging population trend.

name: Statistics Canada – Population Projections for Canada, Provinces and Territories, 2025 to 2075
desc: Official long-range demographic projections covering moderate (57.4M by 2075) and low-growth scenarios, fertility, mortality, and migration assumptions.

name: Statistics Canada – 2021 Census of Population: Ethnocultural and Religious Diversity (Topic Hub)
desc: Primary census data hub for 2021 religious and ethnocultural composition, showing 53.3% Christian, 34.6% no religion, 4.9% Muslim, and 5% Indigenous identity population.

name: Statistics Canada – 2021 Census of Population: Language (Topic Hub)
desc: Primary census data hub for 2021 language composition showing English first official language spoken by 75.5% and French by 21.4% of the population.

name: Statistics Canada – Indigenous Population Profile, 2021 Census of Population
desc: Census profile for the 1.8 million Indigenous persons (5.0% of population) covering First Nations, Métis, and Inuit with age, gender, and socio-demographic characteristics.

name: Pew Research Center – Religious Composition by Country, 2010–2020
desc: Pew modelled estimates of Canada's 2020 religious composition (Christians 53.3%, unaffiliated 34.6%, Muslims 4.9%, Hindus 1.5%) for international comparative benchmarking.

name: Statistics Canada – Confidence in Institutions, Canadian Social Survey Q4 2024
desc: Official government survey data on Canadians' institutional confidence (federal government, courts, police, media) collected November–December 2024.

name: Statistics Canada – Quality of Life Indicator: Trust in Others (Canadian Social Survey 2022–2024)
desc: Longitudinal indicator showing 43.5% of Canadians reported most people can be trusted in Q4 2024, providing interpersonal social trust baseline for cohesion analysis.

name: World Values Survey – Canada, Wave 7 (2017–2022) Data Catalog
desc: WVS Wave 7 micro-data for Canada providing citizen self-report measures of interpersonal trust, institutional confidence, national identity, and political values.

name: Freedom House – Canada: Freedom in the World 2026 Country Report
desc: Annual political rights and civil liberties assessment for Canada for 2026, covering electoral integrity, media freedom, judicial independence, and minority rights.

name: World Justice Project – Canada: WJP Rule of Law Index 2025 Country Fact Sheet
desc: WJP fact sheet showing Canada ranked 13th out of 143 countries on the Rule of Law Index 2025, with sub-scores on constraints on government, absence of corruption, open government, and civil justice.

name: Transparency International – Corruption Perceptions Index 2025
desc: Annual CPI placing Canada 16th out of 182 countries with a score of 75/100, an all-time low, reflecting perceived corruption in public sector institutions.

name: V-Dem Institute – Democracy Report 2026: Unraveling the Democratic Era?
desc: V-Dem 2026 democracy report classifying Canada as a Liberal Democracy ranked 23rd globally on the Liberal Democracy Index, with context on regional backsliding trends.

name: SIPRI – Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025 (Fact Sheet)
desc: SIPRI annual fact sheet providing Canada's military expenditure for 2025 in the global context, used to assess Canada's defence burden relative to NATO commitments.

name: Department of National Defence – Departmental Results Report 2024–25
desc: Official DND annual results report detailing CAF missions, NORAD modernization investments ($38.6B over 20 years), personnel readiness, and Arctic security operations.

name: Parliamentary Budget Office – Planned Capital Spending Under Canada's Defence Policy: 2025 Update
desc: Independent cost analysis of DND's 20-year capital plan ($322.9B total), including the $81.8B Budget 2025 defence announcement and NATO 2% GDP commitment pathway.

name: Canadian Global Affairs Institute – The Diplomat's Guide to Canada 2026
desc: Policy institute primer on Canada's 2026 foreign and defence posture: Arctic investment, EU Security and Defence Partnership, Five Eyes, NATO, trade diversification strategy.

name: Global Affairs Canada – Diversifying Trade for Canada
desc: Official government page on Canada's 15 free trade agreements covering 51 countries, Indo-Pacific Strategy, CPTPP, CETA, and trade diversification objectives beyond the US.

name: UN Comtrade – Canada Trade Flows
desc: UN Comtrade database providing Canada's detailed annual merchandise export and import statistics by product and partner country for multi-year external vulnerability analysis.

name: Statistics Canada – International Trade Statistics Portal
desc: Statistics Canada's portal for monthly and annual merchandise and services trade data, showing April 2026 total trade at $92.9B and partner/commodity breakdowns.

name: Parliamentary Budget Office – Demographic Implications of the 2026–2028 Immigration Levels Plan
desc: PBO analysis of the 380,000 annual PR target, NPR population reduction to under 5% of population by end-2027, and projected demographic and fiscal implications.

name: Government of Canada – Budget 2025: Our Plan: Building Canada Strong
desc: Federal budget introducing $81.8B defence spending over 5 years, productivity super-deduction, $25B Canada Strong sovereign wealth fund, and housing and infrastructure agenda.

name: House of Commons of Canada – Party Standings
desc: Authoritative current distribution of seats among parties in the House of Commons. As of June 2026: Liberal 173, Conservative 140, Bloc Québécois 21, NDP 5, Green 1, Independent 1, 2 vacant — 343 seats total; Liberal 173 of 343 constitutes a majority.

name: CBC News – Carney clinches a majority government with 3 Liberal byelection wins
desc: Reports the Liberals reaching a 174-seat majority on 14 April 2026 via three by-election wins combined with five floor crossings (four Conservative, one NDP); notes it is the first time a PM has reached a majority partly through floor crossing, and the Conservative opposition's contestation of its legitimacy.
